facts.name: California Poppy
facts.color: Orange or yellow, also red, cream or white (orange shown)
facts.light: Full sun; lean, sandy or well-drained soil
facts.notes: Silky orange cups over feathery blue-green leaves; the flowers close at night and on cloudy days. Bees love it. Sow the seed right where it will grow (it doesn't like being moved), and snip off seed pods if you don't want it coming up all over next year.
facts.toxSrc: UC ANR lists the whole plant as toxic if eaten; ASPCA doesn't list it

sources.title: MIgardener (Michigan seed company): California Poppy
sources.note: Eschscholzia californica seed sold by a Michigan company with a store in St. Clair, MI; full sun, easily self-seeds.

sources.title: Oregon State University Extension: California poppy
sources.note: Low-spreading to upright, 6 inches to 2 feet tall; visited by bumble bees, many small native bees and butterflies.

sources.title: UC ANR: Plant Safely, Eschscholzia californica
sources.note: The entire plant is toxic if eaten; supervise pets and children near it.

sources.title: Rutgers NJAES: Landscape Plants Rated by Deer Resistance (printable list)
sources.note: Annuals: calendula and strawflower are rated A (rarely damaged); California poppy, verbena and zinnia B (seldom severely damaged); cosmos C (occasionally severely damaged).

companions.why: Poppies go well with drought-tolerant plants such as lavender and sedum; California poppy needs lean, dry partners.
